commits.message:
fix(search): support Unicode whole-word boundaries

buildSearchPattern wrapped whole-word queries with JavaScript's \b, which
uses ASCII \w semantics. It could not recognize word boundaries around
CJK, Cyrillic, accented letters, or combining marks, so a whole-word
search for e.g. 世界 would not match 你好，世界！.

Replace the ASCII boundary with Unicode-aware lookaround assertions
built from \p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_, and add the `u` flag only when wholeWord
is enabled so the property escapes are interpreted and non-whole-word
searches keep their existing flags and regexp behavior unchanged.

findSearchMatches and replaceAllMatches continue to share the same
compiled pattern, so search and native replacement (capture groups,
$1/$&) stay in sync.

fix(search): validate whole-word regexp queries before wrapping

An already-invalid caller-supplied regexp query (e.g. an unterminated
character class like "[bad(") is normally rejected by buildSearchPattern.
But wrapping it with the whole-word boundary assertions can concatenate
the query's dangling "[" with a "]" from the assertion text, silently
producing a technically valid pattern that matches unintended, arbitrary
text instead of falling back to the documented invalid-regexp contract.

Validate the caller-supplied body compiles on its own, under the same
flags, before wrapping it for whole-word matching. This also gives the
"legacy escape becomes invalid under the Unicode flag" case (e.g. "\a")
a single, explicit place where it resolves to the invalid-regexp
fallback rather than relying on the final construction to catch it.

test(search): cover Unicode boundary edge cases

Extend coverage for the whole-word rewrite: Cyrillic, precomposed
accented Latin, Hangul, a base letter followed by a combining mark,
consecutive combining marks, astral-plane letters with exact UTF-16
offsets, digit/underscore identifiers, start/end-of-document and CRLF
boundaries, adjacent emoji, a punctuation-containing literal query, a
zero-width regexp query, capture groups combined with alternation, and
$1/$& replacement templates.

docs(search): document matching semantics

Add packages/plugin-search/README.md: install, panel + standalone
usage, the Unicode whole-word boundary rules with worked examples, the
whole-word regexp Unicode-mode constraint, the invalid-regexp fallback
contract, and the exported API surface. Every code sample is verified
against the built package rather than hand-derived.
